question.text: A rocket is launched straight upwards from ground level with an effective upward acceleration of 10 m/s². Its propellant burns out completely after 1 min, after which the rocket keeps ascending freely under gravity. Take g = 10 m/s².

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Determine the maximum altitude reached by the rocket above the ground.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Calculate the time elapsed from the moment the fuel burns out until it reaches this maximum altitude.

conditions: starts from rest at ground level
constant net upward acceleration = 10 m/s² during powered phase
free flight under gravity after engine cutoff

solution.approach: Find the speed and height reached at the end of the 1 minute of powered flight, then treat the rest of the rise as free motion decelerating under gravity alone.

steps.text: During the powered phase, the rocket starts from rest and accelerates at 10 m/s² for 60 s. Find the speed and height reached at burnout.
After the fuel finishes, only gravity acts, so the rocket decelerates at g = 10 m/s² until its speed falls to zero.
Find the extra height gained while decelerating from 600 ms⁻¹ to rest.
Add the two heights for the maximum height above the ground.

final_answer.value: (a) maximum height = 36000 m (36 km), (b) time from fuel finish to maximum height = 60 s

common_mistakes.text: Stopping the calculation at burnout and treating 18000 m, the height at fuel finish, as the maximum height, missing that the rocket keeps rising after the fuel runs out.
